title: Canonical unbounded etale compact-support compositor
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be morphisms of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix the compactifications selected by the compactifiability structures on $f$, $g$, and $g\circ f$ [def-asd-compactifiable] [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and suppose $f$ and $g\circ f$ are quasi-compact [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the constant-$A$ etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the compact-support candidates $F_h^c=Rp_*Dj_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Define the canonical compositor $F_fF_g\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{g\circ f}$, with functor products written in left-to-right order, by the proper/open tower construction of Stacks 0F7J and 0F7B(b): writing $d$ for the selected compactification of $g$ and $e$ for that of $g\circ f$, form $a=e.\operatorname{ofComp}(d)$ and its restricted compactification $a.\operatorname{restrict}$ of $f$. First use the inverse canonical compactification comparison $F_f\cong F_f^{a.\operatorname{restrict}}$ whiskered by $F_g$; then use the proper/open tower isomorphism $F_f^{a.\operatorname{restrict}}F_g^d\cong F_{g\circ f}^{d.\operatorname{comp}(a)}$; finally use the canonical comparison $F_{g\circ f}^{d.\operatorname{comp}(a)}\cong F_{g\circ f}$. The tower isomorphism is assembled from the proper/open interchange, direct-image composition and open-extension composition; its map is the specified canonical construction, not an arbitrary isomorphism of these functors. This node introduces that composite, without asserting its further associativity, unit or refinement coherence equations.

def unboundedEtaleLowerShriekCompIso
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    [HasCompactification f] [HasCompactification g] [HasCompactification (f ≫ g)]
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiCompact (f ≫ g)] :
    rightDerivedLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f ⋙
        rightDerivedLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) g ≅
      rightDerivedLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) (f ≫ g)
